1.support: The aim of this study was to report on a single institution's use of esophageal pressure monitoring in burn-injured patients with worsening ARDS

2.support: Adult patients with severe burn injuries with or without smoke inhalation injury admitted to an ABA-verified burn center from January 2017 to May 2024 ... Patients less than 18 years of age, died prior to manometry placement or were designated as comfort care

3.support: Patients were severely injured with a median (IQR) percent total body surface area (TBSA) burned of 39.8% (25.9-59.0), revised Baux score of 91.6

4.support: Per institution protocol, patients who developed ARDS and had worsening oxygenation ... underwent esophageal pressure monitoring; whether every eligible patient actually received Pes during 2017-2024 cannot be determined retrospectively.

5.support: This was a single-center retrospective study with a small sample size, and as a result is not necessarily generalizable to the wider population
5.location: Page 6, Discussion (limitations); no sample size/power calculation reported in Statistical analysis, page 3

6.support: A 16 Fr adult orogastric tube with an inflatable esophageal balloon was used (SmartCath Nasogastric Tube, Carefusion, Yorba Linda, CA)... advanced orally into the mid-lower third of the esophagus

7.support: The primary outcomes sought in this study were to assess necessary ventilatory changes guided by esophageal pressure monitoring. Additional secondary outcomes of interest included trends in oxygenation and resolution of ARDS.
7.location: Page 3, left column, end of manometry section

8.support: No blinding or masking of outcome assessors is described anywhere in the report; in this retrospective review the investigators assessing outcomes were part of the care team aware of Pes status.
8.location: Whole report, Methods and Data collection and analysis (pages 2-3); absence of any blinding statement

9.support: as not all patients had outcomes of interest at each time point, a mixed-effect model for repeated measures followed by Tukey's post-hoc test was used

10.support: For oxygenation trends ... a mixed-effect model for repeated measures followed by Tukey's post-hoc test was used to examine differences at the 4 time points in the least square means of the P/F ratio and PEEP

11.support: Oxygenation was determined prior to Pes use, and at 1-, 3- and 5-day intervals following initiation; only a single pre-intervention measurement is reported, not multiple pre-intervention measures (interrupted time-series).

12.support: The intervention (esophageal pressure monitoring-guided PEEP titration) was applied at the individual patient level, not at a group level.

nih.rationale: Fair rather than Good because of key weaknesses: the sample was small with no power calculation (item 5), not all eligible patients could be confirmed enrolled (item 4, CD), outcome assessors were not blinded (item 8), and there was only a single pre-intervention measurement rather than an interrupted time-series design (item 11), so the observed oxygenation improvements could reflect the natural course of ARDS as the authors themselves acknowledge. Strengths included clearly stated objectives and eligibility criteria (items 1-2), a well-described and consistently applied intervention (item 6), valid objective outcomes (item 7), and appropriate paired statistical testing with p values (item 10); the study was otherwise complete with no attrition (item 9), which prevents a Poor rating.
